adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Nigeria (Wikipedia) - criminalisation layer incl. Katsina
adds.summary: Wikipedia's 'LGBTQ rights in Nigeria' (fetched in full via MediaWiki API, cached research/fetched/815928c9a45eeba4.txt) documents the penalty structure relevant to any trans prisoner in Katsina: in the Shari'a-governed northern states punishments range from lashing/caning to capital punishment, and lesbianism (carnal acts or stimulation between women) is punishable by imprisonment or caning in most states with death penalties applied in Kano and Katsina. It also records the cross-dressing layer: men who dress or behave as women face prison or a fine, citing a 20 Jun 2025 Kano court sentence of a TikToker to one year in prison over a cross-dressing video. Placement axis: the article contains no statement on where trans prisoners are housed - no placement rule, no segregation or women's-wing policy, no Katsina prison-administration measure; it is a criminalisation/penalty record, not a housing record.

adds.title: LGBTQ people in prison (Wikipedia) - no Nigeria section
adds.summary: Wikipedia overview article (fetched in full via MediaWiki API, cached research/fetched/58ce7836f80217d1.txt). Full-text scan for 'Nigeria'/'Nigerian' returns zero mentions: the article's jurisdiction coverage (e.g., placement-by-gender-identity norms elsewhere) has no Nigeria entry. Negative evidence: the global overview documents no Nigeria- or Katsina-specific trans-prisoner housing policy, special unit or segregation-for-placement practice.

records.note: no Katsina-specific or Nigeria-specific trans-prisoner housing/placement data found within budget. Wikipedia full-text search 'transgender prisoner Nigeria housing' returned no jurisdiction-specific article - only generic hits (Persecution of transgender people under the second Trump administration, Right to housing, Prisoners' rights, etc.). The only trans-adjacent prison data located: cross-dressing criminalisation carries imprisonment (Kano 2025 one-year sentence cited by the article), and in Shari'a-governed Katsina lesbianism carries the death penalty while same-sex penalties generally range from lashing/caning to imprisonment - a punishment record, not a housing rule. Where trans prisoners are housed in Katsina/Nigeria is undocumented in these sources; flag as a data gap requiring a Nigerian correctional-services or HRW/PRI source.

adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Nigeria (Wikipedia) - Shari'a-state penalty context for Kebbi
adds.summary: Wikipedia's 'LGBTQ rights in Nigeria' (fetched in full via MediaWiki API, cached research/fetched/815928c9a45eeba4.txt) situates Kebbi inside the northern Shari'a block: in Shari'a-governed northern states punishments for same-sex acts range from imprisonment to capital punishment, and lesbianism is punishable by imprisonment or caning in most states with death penalties applied only in Kano and Katsina - i.e., Kebbi sits on the lashing/imprisonment tier rather than the capital tier, consistent with the record's own statute reading. It also documents the cross-dressing layer (prison or fine for men who dress or behave as women; Kano 2025 one-year imprisonment sentence). Placement axis: nothing on where trans prisoners are housed - no housing, segregation or placement rule for Kebbi or Nigeria anywhere in the article.

adds.title: LGBTQ people in Nigeria (Wikipedia) - criminalisation and trans visibility
adds.summary: Wikipedia article (fetched in full via MediaWiki API, cached research/fetched/767cdbb3294908bd.txt) covering the community-facing picture: the Criminal Code criminalises sex acts between men with penalties up to 14 years' imprisonment, gross indecency between men up to 3 years, lesbianism punishable by imprisonment or caning in most states with death in Kano and Katsina, and cross-dressing penalised in some states (Kano up to one year in prison or a fine for men who dress or behave as women; 2025 Kano sentence of a TikToker to one year in prison). The article cites trans-specific coverage ('I feel invisible': The challenges of being trans in Nigeria, Timinepre Cole) but contains no trans-prisoner housing or placement information for Kebbi or Nigeria.

records.note: no Kebbi-specific or Nigeria-specific trans-prisoner housing data found within budget. Wikipedia full-text search 'transgender prisoners Katsina prison' returned a single generic hit (LGBTQ rights by country or territory). Kebbi's operational difference - a parallel Shari'a criminal layer in force since 1 Dec 2000 with death by stoning as the maximum for men's same-sex acts and up to 50 lashes with imprisonment for up to six months for women's - is a penalty record, not a housing rule. No source located within budget documents where trans prisoners are placed in Kebbi or in Nigeria generally; placement axis undocumented, flag as a data gap.
